The graph consists of $4$ parts: the line segment for  $x\in [-2,0]$,  the arc of a quarter-circle for $x\in [0,1]$, the line segment for  $x\in [1,3]$, and  the arc of a quarter-circle for $x\in [3,6].$ Therefore, we can write the integral as follows:

$$
{\int }_{-2}^{6}f(x)\,\text{d}x={{{\int }_{-2}^{0}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{-{A}_{1}}+{{{\int }_{0}^{1}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{-{A}_{2}}+{{{\int }_{1}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{3}}+{{{\int }_{3}^{6}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{4}}
$$

The $1$st integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [-2,0].$ The corresponding region is a right triangle, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1} & =\frac{1}{2}bh \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 2\cdot 1 \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the region lies below the $x$-axis, we have 

$$
{\int }_{-2}^{0}f(x)\,\text{d}x=-{A}_{1}=-1.
$$

The $2$nd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [0,1].$ The corresponding region is a quarter-circle, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{2} & =\frac{1}{4}\pi {r}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\pi \cdot {1}^{2} \\  & =\frac{\pi }{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the region lies below the $x$-axis, we have 

$$
{\int }_{0}^{1}f(x)\,\text{d}x=-{A}_{2}=-\frac{\pi }{4}.
$$

The $3$rd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [1,3].$ The corresponding region is a right triangle, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{3} & =\frac{1}{2}bh \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 2\cdot 3 \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

The $4$th integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [3,6].$ The corresponding region is a quarter-circle, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{4} & =\frac{1}{4}\pi {r}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\pi \cdot {3}^{2} \\  & =\frac{9\pi }{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-2}^{6}f(x)\,\text{d}x & =-{A}_{1}-{A}_{2}+{A}_{3}+{A}_{4} \\  & =-1-\frac{\pi }{4}+3+\frac{9\pi }{4} \\  & =2+2\pi .\end{aligned}
$$
